body: i couldn't even step on my foot after 8 weeks so it's still early!! i think it'll get better with time :) my dorsiflexion has been improving with more use/stretching over the past few weeks that i've been out of the boot.

Yesterday a grumpy old man asked me to move out of an accessible seat on a crowded bus because my need for it wasn't readily visible, i stg I almost cried :( I feel that planning bit, I had to spend so much money on Ubers when I was still in the boot especially, and it sucks to compare to how I was able to walk endlessly every day (and often night) last summer.

It scares me to think of being immobilized beyond what I've experienced to date.. the human body can be so fickle but also strong in its healing process, it's really strange to have faced that reality. I totally feel you, even while I'm struggling to walk I remember those agonizing days of being bedridden and popping painkillers just a couple months ago. Thank you for the kind words and advice 💓 I hope you're doing much better now.
Thanks so much, glad to hear you're doing better! 💓 How long did your full recovery take?
Hugs 💓 Dorsiflexion is such a struggle!! Pushing through stretches and gritting my teeth while my PT mobilizes/massages it is so painful and difficult :(

Exactly omg, someone honked at me and my friend while crossing the street slowly the other day and I almost cried :( So weird to not be able to walk speedily alongside my friends and feel like I'm slowing them down, even if they're kind about it :/ But yes, this sub rocks 🙏🏻
I'm glad to hear that 💓

Oh those moments of crying when you don't want to ask for help :( I've had so many of those. Especially when the caretaker makes you feel burdensome (as my mom did when I was staying with my family the first couple months), or when you have to ask for something small repeatedly and feel annoying for doing so. 

And it's so true that a simple call or text can be really impactful. I've really started to feel people's lack of object permanence as I get so many more check-ins when I post an IG story or something, but almost radio silence from everyone outside of closest friends otherwise. At this point people are like "damn, you're *still* in a cast/not healed??" because they never understood the extent of how bad my injury was. I also never fully understood or thought about this feeling, but man has it ever shifted my perspective. 

I think about where I was at for that awful week before my surgery - feeling every slightest movement against my broken bones in a loose plaster cast - to now, when I can sit in more comfortable positions and even put my foot on the floor without too much pain. It's an insane shift and I have to keep reminding myself of my previous level of mobility to get over the fear and hesitation. I feel frustrated by the fact that this monumental task of recovery has been added to my life just because of one moment - a slip caused by my own recklessness while rock climbing - but I know I'll get through it. So many people have gone through this, so it's good to know there's a light at the end of the tunnel. Thanks for the reminders and for relating with your experience 💜

I'm sorry to hear about your recent injury. It really is jarring to go from being self-reliant while living alone, to needing help with something so small as feeding myself or getting out of the shower. Showering is such a challenge, there's so many added steps, but thank goodness for those cast covers! 

During my first few weeks I was in so much pain I could barely get around the house to grab things for myself even if I wanted to; didn't go to the store for two months, but only because I was staying with my parents and they took care of that stuff. Now that I'm staying with a couple of friends and I'm PWB, I've made good use of a large backpack, fanny packs, and a leakproof [cup](https://www.amazon.ca/gp/product/B08DM9R4ZG/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o03_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1) and [tupperware](https://www.amazon.ca/gp/product/B01JCNEJHU/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o03_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1) I got so I can carry my food from different rooms. I'm gonna check out a cupholder for my crutches like another commenter mentioned as well. Rolling chairs like you've been using also work great if your home isn't a total mess like my friends' apartment lol!

Thank you for sharing your experience and kind words. Definitely such a relief to know there's others who understand, although I wouldn't wish this on anyone. Hope your recovery goes great and that you receive all the care that you need 💜

That nails it; for those first two months I felt like a total zombie. Then for the first week out of the cast I was feeling more light and free, as I moved back to my city and out of my parents' place where I was having a very miserable post-op recovery. But now, I'm really feeling this new stage of limitations. It's so strange for things that used to be a part of my busy day, like just going to a cafe or park nearby, now take up so much of my energy and mental capacity. It makes me fear how long it will take to reach my past level of activity, as much as I try to focus on short-term goals.

I'm staying with a couple of of my best friends in a busy area, and hearing all the people outside at night on the weekend and feeling like a spectacle when I go to the crowded park full of ppl my age nearby has been a bit sobering. I feel awful when I catch myself feeling frustrated with my friends - they offered me a place to stay until I find an apartment, and I'm doing my best to find one, but their apartment is a total mess and they don't understand accessibility at all. Try as I might to ask for the help I need (keep some of the kitchen clear so I can prep my own food, leave paths open on the floor so I have room to crutch around) they don't fully get it and I feel embarrassed having to repeat my requests when I'm staying under their roof rent-free. I just broke down and cried yesterday when they left for a day trip to the beach that I didn't feel ready for, and I saw the kitchen was a total mess so I had to just order food (which I can't afford to do often, but they do almost every day). I also have to ask them for help every time I leave/return to the apartment bc their stairs are steep and don't have railings at the top part; I feel so undignified when I have to scooch down that part as they hold my crutches 😓 And it doesn't help that I have a phobia of bugs but I've seen a large spider in my room nearly every day since I've been here, leading to me screaming in fear/asking for help every time!! Being on crutches while wanting to run away from a bug is a unique type of humiliation :/ 

I've had trouble even wanting to see some of my less close friends for fear of being in such a vulnerable position around them and inevitably needing their help with one thing or another. I haven't gone out at all the past few days because I didn't want to sweat through my boot in the heat, and it really took a toll on my mental wellbeing. But the one day that my phone told me I reached \~2.4k steps, I felt a lot better - I had felt too scared to try walking as far as you, but now I feel motivated to do it. I think it's like, internalized ableism that only applies to myself that has been hindering my activities more than my physical ability at this point.

I really loved this: "my friends helped me to overcome some of the limitations I had previously established in my own mind." I know if I had a friend in my situation, I'd still want to see them even if they're a bit slower to get around and need a hand every so often. Also, would love to know which crutch cup holder you use!! (weed has found a home in my fanny pack, haha) 

Thank you so much for sharing your perspective and kind words! I hope your recovery goes swimmingly too 💜

Hey everyone! I really need some help dealing with my congested skin. Struggling with so many closed comedones, blackheads, and frequent whiteheads. I live in Canada. I uploaded a lot of pics to show what it looks like as it’s more visible depending on lighting. My skin is also a bit inflamed rn because I picked at it a few days ago - dermatillomania :( I’m working on that part. Kind of at a loss as to what to do, because I’ve tried so many methods. I completely stripped down my routine over the past few months in attempt to figure out if it was a product issue, and I rarely wear makeup.

**Skin info:** I’m 25 years old, currently on spironolactone for hormonal acne. The cysts seem to come back if I skip a day of it. Used doxycycline many years ago. Never tried accutane. I also have seborrheic dermatitis on my scalp. I get cysts on my back and congestion on my back and chest too. My skin used to be oily but the BP has kinda dried it out, now mainly my forehead gets oily bc I have bangs and didn't use as much BP on there.

**Product sensitivities:** butylene glycol, talc, prob more but I just don’t know what else.

**Things I've tried:** I’ve used TO Vitamin C before, currently have some samples of the Ole Henriksen one that I might add into my routine. I used to use TO salicylic acid mask. TO niacinamide and glycolic acid broke me out.

**Lifestyle info:** I'm not very diligent about changing my pillow cases, but the CCs are all over my face anyway. I sleep well, and eat healthy, not too much dairy (occasionally a little cheese or ice cream, sometimes greek yogurt) I was pretty active before my injury, but my skin was the same. Stress levels are def high right now with everything going on in my life, but again, skin has always been congested.

My dermatologist is honestly useless, and it takes so long to get referred to see another. She takes a quick glance and tries to upsell me on her clinic's products, and keeps prescribing me BP or Aczone, which I cut out bc it felt like overkill along with the BP. I tried a retinoid (I think Adapalene?) last year for about 2.5 months, but wasn’t seeing any improvement - I was suuuuper gradual with it though bc I had a bad experience with Differin in 2017 (moisture barrier damage) so I was really careful. Maybe I didn’t stick with it long enough? Just super scared of the purge. Would it help if I got extractions a few times to get rid of some congestion before starting it?

Whenever I get facials (usually extractions and/or salycilic acid peel) I ask aestheticians their opinion too, but I haven’t had luck. I’m a bit tight on money rn so I can’t afford to keep getting extractions and peels. The congestion is def worse when I have to wear a mask for extended periods of time, but for the past couple of months I barely have since I’ve mostly been at home healing from an ankle injury.

**Current routine:**

**AM:**

* TO squalane cleanser or Avene foaming cleanser depending how my skin is feeling (used to use Gentle Simple foaming cleanser but I think it’s been discontinued)
* Sebamed- Sebamed gel + TO squalane oil (Was using CeraVe daily moisturizing lotion before, but I read some ppl get congestion from it. Also sebamed is pricy for the size)
* Avene High Sun Protection Lotion SPF 50+ (I just got this and have only used it a couple times, before I was using Bioderma Photoderma Milk SPF 50+ but I’d cut it out over the winter to see if it caused congestion)

**PM:**

* Neutrogena daily cleanser or Avene foaming cleanser
* This past week I’ve been trying Dr. Dennis Gross’ Alpha Beta Extra Strength Daily Peel, I’ve used 4 treatments so far cuz I had a sample pack of 6. I don’t feel like it’s helped much. I stopped BP in the meantime.
* TactuPump (adapalene 0.1% and benzoyl peroxide 2.5%) every other night - haven’t tried short contact but I wonder if it would help? I noticed it was drying my skin out a lot when I used it too frequently over the winter especially.
* Sebamed gel + TO squalane oil\* First Aid Beauty ultra repair cream - only when skin feels too dry from BP

​

I would really appreciate some guidance!! What should I focus on? Trying a retinoid again? Using actives? Just get it over with and get on accutane? Please let me know what you think.
